Loaded: thermal battery delivery temperature, round-trip efficiency, capex components (input equipment 100 USD/kW-in, heat delivery 300 USD/kW-out, storage medium 5 USD/kWh [1.5-10], storage material up to 10 USD/kWh, price-hunting input incl. grid 110 USD/kW-in), CRF 14%, storage durations (as capacity in h), levelized cost of heat for 2 generation-following and 2 price-hunting cases; comparison efficiencies (gas 75/40/90%, electric immersion ~100%, heat pump COP 2.5, induction/arc 90%, dielectric 70%, laser 30-50%, fleet-average boilers 80%, HP 250%, non-boiler 60%, electric mix 95%), heat-pump max 165 degC (reprinted from Rissman 2022), NREL 100 hp boiler 53,860 USD (reprinted from Jadun et al. 2017), Li-ion 150 USD/kWh and ~80% RTE. Future costs (40 USD/kW, 1.5 USD/kWh, 27 USD/kWh) in _projections. LCOH components, curtailment, charge rates, electricity prices, energy-only comparison heat costs and policy figures in _other-values. NOT printed, so not loaded: battery lifetime or cycle life, fixed/variable O&M, TRL, gas/electric boiler capex per kW or O&M. No full LCOH for gas/electric boilers/heat pumps: Figure 11 comparison costs are energy-only (capital excluded) so kept in _other-values. CAELP/E3 2024 check: this report prints 300 $/kW-out (heat delivery equipment) and 5 $/kWh (storage medium) on printed p.16 (PDF p.17), and 36 h storage for the Texas generation-following battery on p.19; E3's 480 $/kW = 300 + 5 x 36 omits the 100 $/kW-in input equipment component that this report also prints on p.16. Page numbers are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 1).

1. Price year for the capex inputs ($100/kW-in, $300/kW-out, $5/kWh) is not printed beside them; 2023_USD is taken from the Figure 13 caption (p.26, "2023 thermal battery capital costs") and the Figure 10/11 axes ("2023 USD per MWh Thermal Output"). 2. Table 2 (p.27) prints "$/MWh" with no currency year for mixed 2020/2022 electricity prices and capital; loaded as USD/MWh. 3. Storage-material "up to $10/kWh" (p.14) and the $27/kWh long-term figure carry no price year. 4. Capex components state no cost basis beyond the equipment named (no installation, EPC or owner costs mentioned). 5. No lifetime is given; CRF 14% is given as equivalent to two different rate/term pairs (7%/10 yr or 11%/15 yr). 6. Key performance values (95% RTE, 1500-1700 degC, <1%/day losses, $10/kWh) rest on a private Q&A with Antora Energy (ref 11) and a private review (ref 13), not public documents. 7. Figure 11 error-bar bounds are drawn but not printed. 8. Generation-following and price-hunting costs assume perfect foresight / optimal sizing, stated as lower bounds (p.15). 9. The CAELP/E3 480 $/kW derivation labels 300 $/kW as "power" cost, whereas this report prints it as heat delivery equipment per kW thermal output, with a separate 100 $/kW electric-input component.
